chunks: Everything in this book that is narrated from Abdullah ibn Sulayman has been transmitted by me from Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan - may Allah be pleased with him - from Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan Al-Saffar, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Safwan ibn Yahya and Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr together, from Abdullah ibn Sulayman.

key_terms.صَفْوَانَ بْنِ يَحْيَى: Safwan ibn Yahya, a narrator in the chain
key_terms.عبد اللَّهِ بْنِ سُلَيْمَانَ: Abdullah ibn Sulayman, a key narrator
key_terms.مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ: Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr, a narrator in the chain
key_terms.مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْحَسَنِ: Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan, a primary transmitter
key_terms.مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْحَسَنِ الصَّفَّارِ: Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan Al-Saffar, a narrator in the chain

ai.seo_question: How is the narration chain for Abdullah ibn Sulayman verified in this text?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq clarifies the isnad for narrations of Abdullah ibn Sulayman, distinguishing between those he personally transmitted and those derived from his teachers, specifically Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan and Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan Al-Saffar. This meticulous verification underscores the rigorous standards of hadith authentication in Shia scholarship, ensuring the reliability of the Imami tradition by tracing the lineage back to the Imams through trusted companions.
